audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart read Akshan/Skill/Skill/Skill/Fizz/Skill/Skill while content win[] and packet.levelChart both read Fizz/Akshan/Akshan/Skill/Fizz/Fizz/Fizz. Five of seven rows disagreed across layers. breakdown.early also called Akshan's kit 'his CC' — Akshan has no CC in his kit at all.
audit.why: Fizz has the level 1 edge before Avengerang is levelled; 2-3 belong to Akshan because Avengerang is 850 range against a 550 Q and Going Rogue drops to 10s at rank 3, so every commit is escaped; 4-5 are even; from 6 Chum the Waters reveals the camouflage and the lane is Fizz's.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides moved onto the content values with whys rewritten to match. breakdown.early restated on camouflage, which is the actual lane-defining tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and breakdown.spikes asserted the string 'one-shots squishies' with no source; report[8].t told the player to 'add anti-heal early into his sustain' when nothing in Akshan's kit heals.
audit.why: Riot's Going Rogue text grants camouflage, Move Speed and Mana Regen — no healing. His passive grants a shield every third hit, not sustain. Neither champion's text carries damage magnitudes.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal advice replaced with Zhonya's against a stored Comeuppance; magnitudes replaced with the real spike shape — level 3 pole, level 6 reveal, first item beating his auto scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate fabrications about Comeuppance: content.mid, spikes[3].text, whys[6] and wants.foe[1] all called it an EXECUTE, and wants.foe[1] called it GLOBAL. content.mid also said Chum the Waters 'roots on landing'. wants.foe[0] named a non-existent ability, 'Ping-Pong reset healing off camo'. content.early credited Going Rogue with a heal.
audit.why: Riot's Comeuppance text: he stores bullets and fires them, 'dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit' — missing-health scaling at 2500 range, not an execute and not global, and a minion in the path eats it. Fizz's R slows then knocks up; it does not root. Akshan's real ability names are Dirty Fighting, Avengerang, Going Rogue, Heroic Swing, Comeuppance.
audit.corrected: Comeuppance restated as missing-health damage at 2500 range that the first unit hit absorbs. R restated as reveal plus knockup. Invented names and the phantom heal removed. Added the missing interaction the page never carried: Chum the Waters reveals him out of Going Rogue's camouflage, which is the answer to his entire escape pattern. Also added that Heroic Swing needs terrain to grapple, so open lane denies it.
sources: enemyKit E text ('fires a grappling hook into terrain')

audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, Going Rogue 18/14/10/6/2, Avengerang 9/8/7/6/5, Comeuppance 100/85/70. The Going Rogue rank curve is the single most useful number in this lane — it collapses from 18s to 2s.
audit.corrected: All four cooldowns written into the field, with the terrain requirement on Heroic Swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.corrected: Rewritten to their own titles — the terrain requirement on Heroic Swing, and holding E's untargetable frames for a fired Comeuppance.

edits.before: You trade evenly to start, but Akshan's Avengerang (Q) poke plus his Going Rogue (W) camouflage/heal window let him harass you and vanish before you can punish, giving him the edge through levels 2-4. edits.before: Level 6 is close to even but starts trending back your way — his Comeuppance (R) is a scary global execute against low-HP allies, but your own Chum the Waters gives you a reliable way to force fights he can't easily escape, since it roots on landing. From here your all-in speed and burst combo start to outpace his kit; look for picks when his W is down and press advantages with your E dodge to avoid his Avengerang poke chip.

notes:
CHART: content win[] matched packet.levelChart exactly and the full layer disagreed on five of seven rows, so the full layer was the wrong one. The five side edits carry no paired win[N] edit because win[N] already holds the correct value on disk — an edit there would be a no-op the applier rejects. Rows 3 (Skill) and 4 (Fizz) already agreed. After this applies the two layers match.

BOTH suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Chum the Waters' and 'Seastone Trident' are Fizz's real R and W. The real name defect was in wants.foe[0], which invented 'Ping-Pong reset healing off camo' — no such ability, and Going Rogue does not heal.

BIGGEST FIX: four fields called Comeuppance an execute and one called it global. Riot's text is missing-health damage to the FIRST champion, minion or structure hit, at 2500 range — a minion in the way absorbs it. That is a materially different threat model and the page had it wrong everywhere it appeared.

FOCUS FIELD — QUESTION FOR THE USER, not changed: focus.text (and therefore the loading tip and report[5]) names 'Akshan Heroic Swing' as the tracked ability, but the ability that actually decides this lane is Going Rogue (W), which drops from 18s to 2s and is what lets him escape every commit before level 6. Changing focus.text means re-pointing loading, report[5] and dosFull[0].d at the same time. Should focus.text for fizz_mid vs akshan move from Heroic Swing to Going Rogue? I left all four alone rather than half-move them.
